description: Provider-call outcomes, terminal latency, and measured token reporting for Audrey. Calls are not chat turns; absent usage is unknown. No costs are estimated.

panels.description: How to interpret model telemetry before comparing models.

options.content:
**Provider calls are not chat turns.** One turn can call several models. Active calls are not counted yet.

**Usage is measured.** Missing fields stay unknown; reported zero stays zero. Output may include reasoning. Cached input is a subset, not measured cost savings.

**Read each window.** Counter panels show totals since backend restart; charts use the selected range. Rates need multiple scrapes. Latency is a histogram estimate.

panels.title: Reading this dashboard

panels.description: Current histogram counts by model and terminal outcome: ok confirms provider completion, error includes unconfirmed end/failure, cancelled means interrupted before terminal. These are provider calls, not chat turns or visible answers, and exclude calls still in progress. Counts reset with the backend process; the dashboard time picker does not change this current-counter panel. Absent outcome series stay absent, rather than claiming zero.
panels.title: Provider calls since backend restart

panels.description: Recorded provider calls per second, by model and outcome, over $__rate_interval. Rate is calculated before aggregation so backend counter resets are handled. An ok terminal can still represent a length-limited answer; this is not an answer-quality or chat-turn rate. No observations and insufficient scrape history stay no data.
panels.title: Provider terminal rate

panels.description: Estimated median time from starting the provider request until completion, failure, or cancellation, combined across all three outcomes for each model. This excludes earlier pipeline/GPU queue time and later consumer cleanup; it is not first-token or end-to-end chat latency. Uses $__rate_interval and classic histogram buckets with le preserved. Empty windows are omitted. The largest finite bucket is 180 seconds, so a longer tail cannot be resolved above that boundary.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (model, le) (rate(audrey_model_seconds_bucket{job="audrey",model=~"${model}",outcome=~"ok|error|cancelled"}[$__rate_interval]))) and on (model) (sum by (model) (rate(audrey_model_seconds_count{job="audrey",model=~"${model}",outcome=~"ok|error|cancelled"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Provider terminal latency · p50

panels.description: Estimated 95th percentile of provider-terminal latency, combining completed, failed, and cancelled calls per model. Compare with terminal outcome/rate panels: a timeout or cancellation can change this distribution. It does not measure first token, queue wait, or whole-chat latency. Empty windows are omitted. Buckets are coarse and the last finite bucket is 180 seconds; p95 cannot resolve a tail beyond that boundary.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (model, le) (rate(audrey_model_seconds_bucket{job="audrey",model=~"${model}",outcome=~"ok|error|cancelled"}[$__rate_interval]))) and on (model) (sum by (model) (rate(audrey_model_seconds_count{job="audrey",model=~"${model}",outcome=~"ok|error|cancelled"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Provider terminal latency · p95

panels.description: Recorded errors / (ok + error) calls over $__rate_interval, by model. Cancellations are excluded from both numerator and denominator. A zero is supplied only when non-cancelled calls are measured and no error series exists; it means no recorded errors, not unknown token usage. The positive denominator guard leaves no-call windows and absent metrics as no data. This detects provider/transport failures, not incorrect answers.

targets.expr: ((sum by (model) (rate(audrey_model_seconds_count{job="audrey",model=~"${model}",outcome="error"}[$__rate_interval])) or on (model) (0 * sum by (model) (rate(audrey_model_seconds_count{job="audrey",model=~"${model}",outcome=~"ok|error"}[$__rate_interval])))) / on (model) sum by (model) (rate(audrey_model_seconds_count{job="audrey",model=~"${model}",outcome=~"ok|error"}[$__rate_interval]))) and on (model) (sum by (model) (rate(audrey_model_seconds_count{job="audrey",model=~"${model}",outcome=~"ok|error"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Provider error fraction · cancellations excluded

panels.description: Calls interrupted before a provider terminal, per second and model, over $__rate_interval. A consumer closing after an observed terminal does not become a cancellation. Cancellations do not enter the error-fraction denominator. An absent cancelled series stays no data; it is not synthesized as zero.
panels.title: Provider cancellation rate

panels.description: Provider-reported tokens per second for input, output, and cached_input, by model. Each kind appears only when its usage-observation rate is positive in the same window. Thus a valid reported zero appears as zero, while calls omitting the field do not create a zero-token line. Partial coverage can undercount total usage; read coverage alongside this panel. Output may include reasoning. Cached input is a subset, not extra input or proven billing savings. No token estimates or prices are used.

targets.expr: sum by (model, kind) (rate(audrey_model_tokens_total{job="audrey",model=~"${model}",kind=~"input|output|cached_input"}[$__rate_interval])) and on (model, kind) (sum by (model, kind) (rate(audrey_model_usage_observations_total{job="audrey",model=~"${model}",kind=~"input|output|cached_input"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Reported token rate · observed fields only

panels.description: Valid usage observations for a kind / all recorded provider calls for that model, over $__rate_interval. The denominator includes ok, error, and cancelled calls; a confirmed error terminal can report usage, while an interrupted call usually cannot. Each input/output/cached_input field has its own observation count. A reported zero counts as an observation. No observation series is unknown and stays absent; a known series with no new observations during measured traffic can show 0% coverage. No-call windows are omitted. Coverage measures reporting, not cache hit rate, correctness, or billing savings.

targets.expr: sum by (model, kind) (rate(audrey_model_usage_observations_total{job="audrey",model=~"${model}",kind=~"input|output|cached_input"}[$__rate_interval])) / on (model) group_left() (sum by (model) (rate(audrey_model_seconds_count{job="audrey",model=~"${model}",outcome=~"ok|error|cancelled"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Usage reporting coverage · by field

panels.description: Current provider-reported token counters by model and kind, shown only for fields with at least one valid usage observation. A valid measured zero is retained; an unreported field is absent. The counters reset when the backend process restarts and are not totals for the dashboard's selected time range. Counts may cover only part of the calls; check the observations and coverage panels. Output may include reasoning; cached_input is a subset of input, never add it to input when totaling usage. These are not billed-cost estimates.

targets.expr: sum by (model, kind) (audrey_model_tokens_total{job="audrey",model=~"${model}",kind=~"input|output|cached_input"}) and on (model, kind) (sum by (model, kind) (audrey_model_usage_observations_total{job="audrey",model=~"${model}",kind=~"input|output|cached_input"}) > 0)

panels.title: Reported tokens since backend restart

panels.description: Current count of provider calls reporting a valid native token count, separately for input, output, and cached_input. A reported integer zero increments this counter; a missing, malformed, or invalid count does not. This is the evidence behind the token-counter panels. Counts reset with the backend process and are not limited to the selected dashboard time range. Absent fields stay no data.
